raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Settle in.","source_id":"GLUE_PACING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"You're on the Île de la Cité.","source_id":"SYNTHESIZED_OPENER","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"When you're ready, make for Pont Neuf, just ahead.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Look to the middle of the bridge, where Henri IV rides in bronze.","source_id":"GLUE_STAGING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Before that statue was sealed in 1818, the sculptor François-Frédéric Lemot slipped four boxes inside it.","source_id":"c4cd77d6-2377-4371-b394-fb724d0d47ac","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"One holds a history of Henri IV's life, one a 17th-century parchment certifying the first statue, one a note on how this new one was ordered, and the last a list of everyone who paid for it.","source_id":"c4cd77d6-2377-4371-b394-fb724d0d47ac","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The first Henri IV had been torn down in 1792, and when the Bourbons returned they recast him from a surviving mould of the original.","source_id":"c4cd77d6-2377-4371-b394-fb724d0d47ac","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The bronze itself was melted down from a statue of Desaix.","source_id":"c4cd77d6-2377-4371-b394-fb724d0d47ac","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Steps beside the statue lead down to the square du Vert Galant, where Jacques de Molay, Grand Master of the Templars, was burnt at the stake — cursing the kings as the flames took him.","source_id":"1311c7fd-d25d-492b-b51c-acf1d91cabf7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Just off the bridge sits the Place Dauphine, and once a year it turned into a salon for the unknown.","source_id":"70582f12-4829-4b52-8dfd-9f3672362754","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"On the Petite Fête-Dieu, the 'Small Corpus Christi' eight days after the main feast, young painters hung their canvases here from six in the morning until noon.","source_id":"70582f12-4829-4b52-8dfd-9f3672362754","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"It was unofficial, a chance for nobodies to be seen — a forerunner of the Salon des Refusés that would later spark the Impressionists.","source_id":"70582f12-4829-4b52-8dfd-9f3672362754","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"In 1720 a twenty-two-year-old, son of the man who kept the king's billiards, showed an antique bas-relief.","source_id":"70582f12-4829-4b52-8dfd-9f3672362754","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"J.-B. Vanloo stopped, studied it a long while, found real qualities in it, bought it, and took the young man under his wing.","source_id":"70582f12-4829-4b52-8dfd-9f3672362754","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Eight years on, that painter was Vanloo's colleague at the Academy of Painting.","source_id":"70582f12-4829-4b52-8dfd-9f3672362754","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"His name was Jean-Baptiste-Siméon Chardin.","source_id":"70582f12-4829-4b52-8dfd-9f3672362754","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Along the sides of the bridge run three hundred and eighty-one carved stone faces, no two alike.","source_id":"f72c949c-d423-4715-892e-cbdabde0475d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"They're forest and field gods from old myth, satyrs and sylvains, copied from originals attributed to the Renaissance sculptor Germain Pilon.","source_id":"f72c949c-d423-4715-892e-cbdabde0475d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Pilon also carved the tomb of Henry II and Catherine de'Medici at Saint-Denis.","source_id":"f72c949c-d423-4715-892e-cbdabde0475d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"His originals lasted until the bridge was completely rebuilt between 1851 and 1854.","source_id":"f72c949c-d423-4715-892e-cbdabde0475d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Six went to the Musée Carnavalet, eight more to the Cluny, and today they all sit at the Musée National de la Renaissance at Château d'Écouen.","source_id":"f72c949c-d423-4715-892e-cbdabde0475d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The copies here now were cut by Maindron, Lavigne, Barye and Fontenelle — and Fontenelle alone made sixty-one, on the upstream side between the right bank and the Île de la Cité.","source_id":"f72c949c-d423-4715-892e-cbdabde0475d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"That's Pont Neuf — Henri IV in bronze, with four boxes hidden inside.","source_id":"GLUE_CLOSING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0}]}
